questions.question: Which spelling is correct when रामम् is followed by a consonant?
questions.explanation: Before a consonant, final म् changes to anusvāra (ं).

questions.question: Which spelling is correct when भक्तम् is followed by a vowel?
questions.explanation: Before a vowel, म् remains unchanged and may either stay separate or join with the following vowel. Both forms are accepted in the handbook.

questions.question: Which sentence is written correctly at the end of a sentence?
questions.explanation: At the end of a sentence, final म् remains unchanged.

questions.question: Which form correctly follows the णत्व rule?
questions.explanation: रामेण is the correct form after applying the णत्व rule.

questions.question: Which word is written correctly?
questions.explanation: The षष्ठी बहुवचन form is रामाणाम्.

questions.question: Which spelling correctly shows परसवर्ण?
questions.explanation: The nasal changes according to the following consonant group.

questions.question: Which sentence is correctly written?
questions.explanation: According to the handbook, Sanskrit word order does not change the meaning of the sentence.

questions.question: Which word correctly follows the णत्व rule?
questions.explanation: नृपेण is the correct तृतीया एकवचन form.

questions.question: Which word is written correctly?
questions.explanation: परिश्रमेण correctly applies the णत्व rule.

questions.question: Which spelling correctly follows the writing rules?
questions.explanation: When रामम् is followed by the consonant ग, final म् changes to anusvāra (ं).

questions.question: Why is रामम् नमति written as रामं नमति?
options: Final म् changes to अनुस्वार before a consonant.
questions.explanation: When a word ending in म् is followed by a consonant, the म् is written as अनुस्वार (ं).

questions.question: Why does रामेण contain ण instead of न?
questions.explanation: The preceding र triggers the णत्व rule in this form.

questions.question: Why does रामाणाम् use ण?
options: णत्व applies in the षष्ठी बहुवचन form.
questions.explanation: The र before न causes न to become ण according to the णत्व rule.

questions.question: In शङ्कर, why is ङ् used?
questions.explanation: Before a क-वर्ग consonant, the anusvāra becomes ङ् according to the परसवर्ण rule.

questions.question: In सञ्जय, why is ञ् used?
questions.explanation: Before a च-वर्ग consonant, the anusvāra changes to ञ्.

questions.question: Why does संसार remain written with ं instead of another nasal?
options: Because the following consonant does not belong to a consonant group requiring परसवर्ण.
questions.explanation: When the following consonant is not one of the grouped consonants, the anusvāra remains unchanged.

questions.question:
Why do all of these sentences have the same meaning?

रामः सूर्यं नमति।
सूर्यं रामः नमति।
नमति रामः सूर्यं।
options: Because Sanskrit word order is flexible.
questions.explanation: The handbook explains that changing word order does not change the meaning of a Sanskrit sentence.

questions.question: Which rule explains the change from संकर to शङ्कर?
questions.explanation: The nasal changes according to the consonant group that follows.

questions.question: Which writing rule is responsible for the change from रामेन to रामेण?
questions.explanation: The preceding र causes न to become ण.

questions.question: Which of the following changes is caused by a different writing rule than the others?
questions.explanation: The first, second, and fourth changes are due to णत्व. The third is due to परसवर्ण.

questions.question: Which pair of words demonstrates the same writing rule?
questions.explanation: Both रामेण and नृपेण follow the णत्व rule.

questions.question: Which word is written using a different writing rule than the others?
questions.explanation: The first three use णत्व. संगच्छति illustrates the final म्/अनुस्वार writing rule.

questions.question: In which situation does a final म् remain unchanged?
questions.explanation: A final म् remains unchanged before a vowel.

questions.question: Which statement about Sanskrit word order is correct?
options: Changing the word order always changes the meaning.
Only the subject may change position.
Word order is generally flexible without changing the meaning.
The verb must always come last.
questions.explanation: The handbook explains that Sanskrit word order is generally flexible.

questions.question: Why do रामेण and रामाणाम् both contain ण?
questions.explanation: In both words, the preceding र causes न to become ण.

questions.question: Which pair illustrates two different writing rules?
questions.explanation: रामेण demonstrates णत्व, while सञ्जय demonstrates परसवर्ण.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the परसवर्ण rule?
options: To change a nasal sound so it matches the following consonant group.
To replace every न with ण.
questions.explanation: परसवर्ण adjusts the nasal to match the consonant that follows.

questions.question: Which writing rule affects the spelling of रामं गच्छति?
questions.explanation: The final म् becomes अनुस्वार before the consonant ग.

questions.question: Which two words illustrate the same writing principle?
questions.explanation: Both शङ्कर and सञ्जय are examples of परसवर्ण.

questions.question: Which feature best distinguishes the णत्व rule from the परसवर्ण rule?
options: णत्व changes न to ण under specific conditions, while परसवर्ण changes the nasal sound to match the following consonant group.
Both rules always produce the same spelling change.
णत्व applies only at the end of a sentence.
questions.explanation: The two rules affect different letters and are triggered by different conditions.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which all writing rules are applied correctly.
options: अहं मित्रेण सह वनं गच्छामि तथा मालाम् आनयामि।

अहं मित्रेन सह वनं गच्छामि तथा मालां आनयामि।
अहम् मित्रेण सह वनम् गच्छामि तथा मालाम् आनयामि।
questions.explanation: अहं and वनं correctly apply the final म् rule; मित्रेण correctly applies णत्व; मालाम् remains unchanged before the vowel आ.
